Amid the crowds, I wonder: if aging and farewell no longer stir the heart, if flowers and cakes bring no anticipation, what separates living from dying? When small beauties cease to move you, the world’s noise means nothing. I learned that a silent spirit is more desolate than a body’s end. Our true ending comes when nothing within us stirs. I may not belong in this world, but only I can pass judgment on my soul.
Rather than the fear that keeps us still, courage—even when reckless—comes closer to a soul that burns.
The windmills of life never stop turning. A true knight does not lower the lance because others laugh.
We are all knights caught in the ordinary world, carrying blood that has not cooled and dreams of dragons yet to face.
What the world calls madness may be our armor against mediocrity, a medal worn by the spirit alone.

What stays deepest in memory is often intangible. Years later, you may forget a face, yet a familiar perfume on a crowded street can make you turn without thinking. You see only strangers walking away. Then you realize that even if it had been her, even face to face, you might no longer have recognized who she has become.
